records.name: presynaptic transmitter identity

value.policy: per-body consensus transmitter from the connectome annotation; unclear stays unresolved

records.applies_to: the presynaptic neuron of a chemical synaptic edge
records.source: project scientific rule; ADR-2026-010; ADR-2026-012; docs/evidence/LITERATURE_PARAMETER_CORPUS.md section 7
records.biological_mismatch: The MaleCNS consensus transmitter is a classifier prediction from electron-microscopy image features, not a measurement of the transmitter a given body releases. Co-transmission is not represented: one label per body, where a real neuron can release a small molecule and a peptide together.
records.uncertainty: This record was narrowed by ADR-2026-012. It previously bundled transmitter identity with the postsynaptic receptor term and was cited wherever an edge sign was asserted, which made an untestable claim look like a tested one. Transmitter identity is testable and now has a reserved validation set: 6,107 verified per-cell-type assignments with a stated evidence class, of which 3,523 rows carry a MaleCNS cell type in the cell_type_mcns column. That set measures how often the transmitter label is right. It cannot measure whether an edge excites or inhibits, which additionally requires ND-10.
records.validation: verified per-cell-type transmitter assignments, joined on cell type at a stated confidence floor. Reserved and unopened; see configs/datasets/stage2-reservations-v1.json.

records.name: postsynaptic receptor identity and functional edge polarity

value.policy: edge sign is a function of the ND-03 transmitter and the postsynaptic receptor; where receptor evidence is absent the sign is unresolved and remains a latent model alternative
value.transmitter_only_sign_rule: a named regression control, not the physiological default

records.source: project scientific rule; ADR-2026-008; ADR-2026-012; docs/evidence/LITERATURE_PARAMETER_CORPUS.md section 7; docs/evidence/TRANSMITTER_SIGN_CONTROL.md
records.biological_mismatch: Receptor class does match the presynaptic transmitter, which is why a transmitter-only sign rule is broadly right. What it cannot capture is that different receptors for the same transmitter localise to different dendritic domains receiving different presynaptic partners, so the sign of an edge is partner-specific rather than cell-specific. Acetylcholine is the clearest case: a cholinergic input can be excitatory through a nicotinic receptor and inhibitory through a muscarinic one at the same postsynaptic cell.
records.uncertainty: This is a boundary, not a pending action. The measurement required is domain-resolved and partner-resolved receptor localisation, which exists for a handful of visual-system neurons and not at connectome scale. No bulk expression atlas can supply it, because the quantity is partner-specific and an atlas reports per-cell-type expression. The MaleCNS receptorType annotation carries 752 non-null entries, all gustatory (ppk23, ppk25, IR52b) and none olfactory. Consequently edge sign is left unresolved wherever receptor-level evidence is absent, and unresolved signs are carried as latent alternatives rather than defaulted. The verified transmitter ground truth reserved for ND-03 does not validate this record: a correct transmitter label still leaves the sign unresolved where the receptor is unknown, so an agreement rate on transmitter identity is an upper bound on sign correctness and not a measurement of it.
records.validation: domain-resolved and partner-resolved receptor localisation together with paired physiology and causal perturbation. Not available at scale, so this record cannot currently be advanced by any work available to this project.

records.name: Track A closed-loop station-keeping controller
records.units: proportional gains in rad per mm of thorax fore-aft error and rad per rad of heading error; integral gains in rad per mm-second and rad per rad-second; offset limits in rad; settle window in microseconds
records.applies_to: the Track A FlyGym body engine while standing under no descending command
records.source: project engineering decision 2026-09-09; gains chosen by the closed-loop sweep recorded in docs/evidence/TRACK_A_STATION_KEEPING.md
records.biological_mismatch: Entirely non-biological. A real fly holds station with load-sensing campaniform sensilla and femoral chordotonal reflexes distributed through the VNC; this is proportional feedback from a single thorax pose estimate onto the femur-tibia pitch of all six legs, which no fly has. It exists because the FlyGym locomotor controller this scaffold is built on has no station-keeping mode, so its open-loop standing pose hold lets a persistent net force integrate at about 0.88 mm/s.
records.uncertainty: The control channel, both gains and the offset limit are engineering choices, not measurements. The channel was selected by measuring the drift response of all six leg joint groups in common and differential mode; femur-tibia pitch had the largest authority in each. The offset limit is load-bearing rather than a safety margin: the measured drift velocity falls from +1.02 mm/s at zero offset through zero near 0.055 rad, but at 0.12 rad it is +1.40 mm/s, worse than no control, so a limit outside the first monotone branch lets the controller saturate onto its own worst operating point. A rate term was implemented and rejected: the smallest gain tried moved the body 5.9 mm instead of 0.36 mm. A signed lateral channel exists and was measured at about 263 mm/rad on differential coxa-trochanter roll; it is deliberately not used, because lateral error is only about 0.7 mm of the worst residual and a gain that large on a contact-mode-switching plant is a stability risk. No claim is made that any of this resembles fly motor control. A second fore-aft channel was implemented and rejected on the development poses. Coxa roll at weight -1.0 looked like a clean win on the three poses it was swept over, cutting the worst 12-second displacement from 3.163 to 1.710 mm, but those three were selected from the failing set: on all seven development poses it is worse overall, at 3.893 mm worst case and 3 of 7 passing against 5 of 7 for no secondary channel. Weight -1.5 passes 6 of 7 but has a worse worst case at 3.315 mm, so choosing it would be fitting seven samples with a hand-set weight. The channel is therefore implemented and registered at weight 0.0, which disables it, and the refutation is recorded rather than the tuning.
records.validation: track-a-acceptance-v4 criterion B2, which it clears at every pose tested. It does not clear B3 as that criterion is written; see docs/evidence/TRACK_A_STATION_KEEPING.md. The controller-only control must still fail to produce the behavioural sequence. Under track-a-acceptance-v5, evaluated once at frozen commit 4c4a53f on twelve poses drawn from seed 20260910 and never seen during tuning: B2 passes 12 of 12 with a worst 3-second displacement of 0.957 mm, and B3-v5 passes 8 of 12 against the 10 required, so validation FAILS. Development was 5 of 7 and validation 8 of 12, the same rate, so this is a capability limit at the twelve-second horizon rather than an overfitting gap. Those twelve poses are spent: they may not be rescored, and they may not be tuned against. A successor controller is registered as MOTOR-05 with a fresh development set and a separately frozen validation set drawn from a new registered seed, both registered before tuning begins, and this failure stays on the record either way.

records.name: observation model for external electrophysiological tests
records.applies_to: scoring a registered synaptic model against a published evoked-EPSC recording
records.biological_mismatch: Every clause is false in detail. A compound evoked EPSC saturates postsynaptic receptors, so amplitude is concave in released vesicles rather than linear; nicotinic receptors desensitise on the timescale of the shortest paired-pulse intervals; and electrical stimulation of an axon bundle does not recruit an identical population on a second pulse milliseconds later. A model resource ratio is therefore not the same object as a measured amplitude ratio, and the difference between them has no fixed sign.
records.uncertainty: AMENDED 2026-09-09, before any reserved value was opened. The first version of this record claimed the three biases all deepen a measured ratio, and concluded that a measured ratio above the prediction could not be explained by observation error. That conclusion is WITHDRAWN and it was wrong in the most consequential direction, because it would have licensed reading a high measured ratio as agreement. Postsynaptic receptor saturation biases a measured paired-pulse ratio UPWARD: the transfer from released vesicles to measured current is concave, so the larger first response is compressed more than the smaller second one, and the measured amplitude ratio exceeds the underlying release ratio. Receptor desensitisation biases it DOWNWARD, because receptors occupied or desensitised by the first pulse are unavailable to the second. Recruitment is not safely one-directional at all: failure of stimulated axons to fire again lowers the ratio, while stimulus-dependent changes in axonal excitability can raise it, and variable recruitment adds variance with no fixed sign. So no measured value is protected from observation error in either direction, and neither agreement nor disagreement with a prediction can be attributed to the model without an independent handle on saturation and desensitisation at this synapse. What survives is weaker and still useful: every one of these effects shrinks as the interstimulus interval grows, because receptor occupancy recovers and the second response no longer rides on the decay of the first.
records.validation: An independent handle on the two postsynaptic terms at this synapse. For saturation, the standard test is a low-affinity competitive antagonist that relieves receptor occupancy without changing release: if the measured paired-pulse ratio falls under it, saturation was inflating the ratio. For desensitisation, a measured recovery time course of the receptor response at fixed release. Failing those, the same paired-pulse ratio measured under minimal and under compound stimulation in one preparation bounds the whole observation term at once. None of the three is registered.
